name: Toyota Chaser (JZX100)
h1: Toyota Chaser (JZX100): specs, 1JZ-GTE engine and what owners say

us.x: Never sold new in the US. JZX100 Chasers began to become legal to import under the 25-year rule in 2021, each car once it is 25 years old by its month of build.

fame.x: Daigo Saito won the 2016 D1 Grand Prix title in a JZX100 Chaser. His first D1 title, in 2008, came in the Mark II version of the same car.

Wikipedia says the Chaser became famous in drifting, mostly because it is front-engined with rear-wheel drive, and many X90 and X100 cars were built into drift cars. Jalopnik says the drift crowd took to it for its JZ engine and rear-wheel drive.
X100 Chasers raced in the Japanese Touring Car Championship in 1997 and 1998. In 1998 the car won the title with Masanori Sekiya and the TOM’S team.
The Chaser, Mark II and Cresta were the same car with different badges, sold through different Toyota dealer chains. Toyota says the Chaser’s overhangs were 45 mm shorter than the Mark II’s.
Car Throttle says it is easy to get a lot more power out of the Tourer V’s 1JZ. Jalopnik says the Chaser ranks seventh on JDMBUYSELL’s list of its 10 most-watched JDM cars.

gens.tag: 2.5-liter single-turbo 1JZ-GTE, 280 PS (276 hp), 5-speed manual or automatic, rear-wheel drive. Japan only.

variants.name: Chaser Tourer V

hp.note: 280 PS at 6,200 rpm, Japan’s gentlemen’s agreement figure (JDM)

tq.note: lb-ft at 2,400 rpm (379 Nm per Wikipedia; Toyota’s catalog says 377.6 Nm, per JDMBUYSELL)

trans.note: R154 manual; ECT-iE automatic. JDMBUYSELL says manual cars had a standard limited-slip differential.

weight.note: manual, Toyota catalog figure via JDMBUYSELL; 1,480 kg with the automatic

variants.what: The sporty top trim. The previous Tourer V’s twin turbos gave way to one turbo with VVT-i. Output stayed at 280 PS, and peak torque came much lower in the rev range.

variants.name: Chaser Tourer S

hp.note: 200 PS at 6,000 rpm (Toyota); Wikipedia gives 197 bhp

tq.note: lb-ft at 4,000 rpm (251 Nm per Wikipedia; Toyota’s catalog says 255 Nm, per JDMBUYSELL)

trans.note: no manual; JDMBUYSELL says a 5-speed automatic came in August 1998

variants.what: The sporty look without the turbo: the 2.5-liter 1JZ-GE with VVT-i.

1JZ-GTE.name: Toyota 1JZ-GTE
facts: 280 PS (276 hp) at 6,200 rpm, 379 Nm (280 lb-ft) at 2,400 rpm in the VVT-i single-turbo version
Two CT12A turbos at launch in 1990; one CT15B turbo with VVT-i from about 1996, as in the JZX100

issues.x: Wikipedia says the first twin-turbo engines use ceramic turbine wheels that can delaminate at high turbo speed and heat. This applies to the early engines, not the single-turbo JZX100 version.

issues.t: Blow-by valve and turbo seals (early engines)
issues.x: On early engines a faulty one-way valve on the intake cam cover let blow-by gas into the intake, and oil vapor reaching the turbos wore their seals early. Wikipedia says Toyota recalled these engines in Japan, but exports were not covered.
JDMBUYSELL’s buyer’s guide quotes Unique Cars: on late five-speed manual Chasers, a hard-driving former owner may have burned out the clutch. Test drive for slip and judder.
JDMBUYSELL says Japan salts its roads, so a Japanese car is not proof of a dry one. Check the underbody, sills, arches and floors.

1JZ-GE.name: Toyota 1JZ-GE
facts: 200 PS (197 bhp) at 6,000 rpm with VVT-i, from 1995
86 x 71.5 mm, 2,492 cc, same as the 1JZ-GTE

issues.x: JDMBUYSELL says Japan salts its roads, so a Japanese car is not proof of a dry one. Check the underbody, sills, arches and floors.
